sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: A branched, tree-like cactus endemic to southern Mexico, reaching about 4–7 m. Its upright branches bear small yellow flowers near their tips.

sections.title: Fruit
sections.text: The fleshy, purple fruits are covered with scales and measure about 5 cm. Their sweet pulp is eaten locally.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: Documented food use concerns the ripe fruit; it does not establish that other parts are edible.

sources.title: Britton & Rose — The Cactaceae, vol. II
